To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
MOR A118G and C17T polymorphisms are associated with opioid dependence and that circulating Ig levels are significantly different in individuals carrying different genotypes of MOR.
the frequency of 118G allele in opiate users was higher than non-users and the mean IgG and Ig A levels were significantly lower in opiate users than in non-users.
opioid addicts show immunosuppression as judged by circulating immunoglobulin levels and that the immunosuppressive effects of opioids are mediated by Mu opiate receptor polymorphism.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of MOR polymorphism in the immunomodulatory effects of opiates.
the correlation of circulating Ig levels and MOR genotypes in opiate users.
the role of MOR genotypes in immunosuppression induced by opiates in their users.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
MOR A allele is associated with opioid dependence and immunosuppression and C allele is associated with immunosuppression only.
the A118G and C17T polymorphisms of the MOR gene do not influence opiate dependence.
118A allele was associated with immunosuppression and 118G allele with immunopotentiation, whereas no such association was found in case of C17 allele.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the MOR gene polymorphisms are correlated with circulating Ig levels in opiate users.
MOR A118G polymorphisms are associated with opiate dependence and immunosuppression.
the MOR gene polymorphism and the circulating Ig levels are associated with opioid dependence and that these associations may be used to predict the risk of addiction.
The main takeaway from our work is that
opioid addiction and MOR polymorphism are associated with immunosuppression.
the 118G allele of MOR is associated with opioid dependence, and individuals with 118G allele show immunosuppression.
opioid users have significantly lower levels of IgG and Ig A as compared to non-users.
